what_its_for: Difluprednate eye drops are used to treat pain, swelling, and redness in the eye after eye surgery. They may also be used to treat a condition called uveitis, which is inflammation inside the eye. This medicine belongs to a group of drugs called corticosteroids, or steroids, which help reduce inflammation in the eye.
how_to_take: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water before using these drops. 2. Shake the bottle well before each use. 3. Tilt your head back and gently pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket. 4. Hold the dropper tip close to your eye but do not touch your eye or eyelid. 5. Squeeze one drop into the pocket of your lower eyelid. 6. Gently close your eye and press lightly on the inner corner of your eye near your nose for about 1 to 2 minutes. This helps keep the medicine in your eye and reduces the amount absorbed into your body. 7. If you are using drops in both eyes, repeat the steps for your other eye. 8. Do not rinse the dropper tip. Replace the cap tightly after each use.
dosing: For eye inflammation and pain after surgery: The usual dose is 1 drop in the affected eye 4 times a day, starting 24 hours after surgery and continuing for 2 weeks. Then the dose is usually reduced to 1 drop twice a day for another week, then 1 drop once a day for the final week. For uveitis: The usual dose is 1 drop in the affected eye 4 times a day for 14 days. Your doctor may slowly reduce your dose over time. Always follow the exact dosing schedule your doctor gives you, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Do not freeze. Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the drops if they look cloudy, discolored, or contain particles.
what_to_avoid: 1. Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye, eyelid, fingers, or any other surface, as this can contaminate the drops and cause an eye infection. 2. Do not wear contact lenses while being treated with this medicine unless your doctor specifically tells you it is okay. 3. Avoid rubbing your eyes. 4. Be careful when driving or doing activities that require clear vision, as this medicine may temporarily blur your vision right after using it. Wait until your vision is clear before driving.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: sudden vision changes or vision loss, eye pain that gets worse, increased redness or swelling in or around the eye, seeing halos or rainbow-colored rings around lights (which may be a sign of increased eye pressure), signs of eye infection such as increased discharge, crusting, or a feeling that something is in your eye, headache or pain around the eyes, or if your symptoms do not improve or get worse after a few days of treatment. Also call your doctor if you accidentally swallow any of the eye drops.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some relief from pain, redness, and swelling within a few days of starting treatment. However, it is very important to continue using the drops exactly as prescribed, even if your eye feels better, until your doctor tells you to stop. Stopping too early may allow the inflammation to come back.
special_populations: Tell your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. For children: The safety and effectiveness of difluprednate in children has not been fully established for all uses; talk to your doctor. For older adults: No special dose adjustment is typically needed, but older patients should report any new vision changes to their doctor promptly. If you have a history of herpes eye infections, glaucoma, cataracts, or diabetes, tell your doctor before using this medicine, as extra monitoring may be needed.
